_doc: The 2 million riders scenario: 2M daily transit trips (each trip counted once, all modes) by 2100. The plan plus the expansion package (arterial BRT grid, SH-114 metro, job-campus BRT, infill stations), the D2 subway, the Red Line on to McKinney, regional rail to Weatherford, Greenville and Cleburne by the 2090s (scenarios/two_million/extra/), the frequent-service package (edits.csv), better access (15-min feeder buses, bike/scooter to stations, walkable station areas, drop-off) and moderate land use (upzoning around stations, 20% of growth steered to station areas). Parking prices double in real terms by 2050 in today's paid districts and $5/day parking spreads to the densest job centers (15,000+ jobs/km2; cash-out is left out). The D2 subway takes the Green and Orange lines off the downtown mall from 2035, and regional rail runs through Fort Worth and Dallas. Stages are scheduled by riders per dollar (staging.priority), so cheap high-value BRT comes early under the same $2.3B/yr budget. Merged over config.json for this scenario only.

staging._doc_rules: Review 2 (owner decision D2): the order is riders per $ (results/two_million/line_values.csv: trips lost when a line is removed from the 2100 network, per $M of its share of capital at 2025 prices; the same whatever order lines open in), with three rules: the stages of plan lines that reach a downtown core (and the stages they need to connect) open no later than in the budget plan (core_by_plan); a county's next line goes ahead of the value order once its share of population (x ratio) of the capital committed so far covers it (fair_share); a new line doesn't open as a stub of fewer than min_starter_stops stops ahead of its next stage. Deadlines: lines that must open by a year.

staging._doc_ride: ride_open_track: a line runs over track another line has already opened as soon as it is open and joins the line's own open track (review 3: I-30 on the I-20 Crosstown's downtown track from 2043, +12.9k trips in 2045). Nothing is built, so nothing is charged.
staging._doc_r3: Review 3 (R3): fair_share.band_years / band_low: a county that got less than half its population share of the capital committed over the last ten years of budget (deadline stages included) goes next with its best line. enforce_interval: no more than max_km_per_interval of a line opens in one year.
